incident-bot: PagerDuty: CRITICAL - edge-proxy-cluster-3 high 502 rate in us-west-2. Page sent to oncall. Auto-created incident #INC-2987.
Sasha Rivera: acked. pulling up LB metrics and proxy logs. ETA 5.
Mike Chen: on it. seeing a spike in backend 502s from target group tg-edge-prod-3. Health shows some targets UNHEALTHY intermittently.
Anya Patel: any recent deploys? CI shows no production deploys in the last 30m.
Sasha Rivera: no deploys. rollout window earlier today was 02:00 UTC. this looks like runtime failure. collecting logs.
Mike Chen: dumping a few logs: ```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z proxy-edge-03 ERR TLS handshake failed: remote error: tls: bad certificate
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z backend-12 502 Bad Gateway: upstream read timeout
2026-03-15T14:02:13Z proxy-edge-03 ERR connection reset by peer
```
Sasha Rivera: TLS handshake errors + backend read timeouts. could be certificate rotation or an ALB target flapping due to healthcheck failures.
Leo Gomez: checking ELB/ALB console now — target group shows 3/6 healthy, failing hosts reporting 503/502 on healthcheck path `/healthz`.
Anya Patel: netops-bot, can you surface recent route53 changes? TTLs?
netops-bot: Route53 change log: no hosted zone updates in last 24h for the edge domain. Last change: 2026-03-14T08:11:02Z (certificate auto-renew).
Sasha Rivera: certificate auto-renew at 03/14 - could there be an incompatibility? but error is "bad certificate" during TLS handshake from proxy -> backend. Are we terminating TLS at proxy and re-establishing to backends?
Mike Chen: yes, we do mutual TLS to backends for auth. If backend certs rotated and some backends have stale chains, handshake will fail and ALB will mark them unhealthy.
Simone (product): any customer-facing impact? support reported a handful of 502 errors from EU customers ~14:02 UTC.
Sasha Rivera: initial impact appears partial. Router-level retries are happening, so some requests succeed after retries. We're seeing elevated error rate but not total outage. marking P2 for now, moving to P1 if error rate crosses threshold.
Mike Chen: I'm SSHing to failing backends to check certs. quick check: on backend-12 `sudo openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:8443 -showcerts` returns certificate chain ending 2026-06-01 — that looks fine. backend-14 chain looks different, expired 2026-03-01.
Anya Patel: expired cert on some backends — that would explain intermittent TLS bad certificate. how did rotation miss those instances?
Leo Gomez: rotation job runs on node boot + periodic cron. looks like backend-14 was not fully patched and missed the restart after rotation. image shows older cert present.
Sasha Rivera: plan: 1) remove unhealthy targets from ALB weight temporarily 2) failover traffic to warm pool in us-west-1 3) rotate cert on stale backends / restart service 4) monitor error rate and pager.
Mike Chen: doing step 1 now: reducing weight for tg-edge-prod-3 failing targets.
Mike Chen: step 1 done. traffic offloaded to healthy nodes in same AZ and warm pool. seeing overall 502 rate drop by ~40%.
Sasha Rivera: step 2: initiating weighted failover to us-west-1 warm pool (30% -> 70%) to reduce latency impact. executing runbook: `./runbooks/failover.sh --region us-west-1 --weight 70`
Sasha Rivera: failover script executed, traffic shifted. monitoring the 1m error rate.
Anya Patel: starting cert rotation on flagged nodes: rolling restart to pick up new cert. `systemctl restart redwood-proxy`
Mike Chen: restarting backend-14 now. health checks are red, but after restart we should pick new cert.
Mike Chen: backend-14 returned healthy after restart. TLS handshake errors for that host cleared.
Sasha Rivera: netops-bot: any DNS propagation surprises? we didn't change DNS but just checking TTLs in case clients cached bad endpoints.
netops-bot: Edge CNAME TTL 60s, no recent change. no DNS anomalies.
Leo Gomez: good. looks cert rotation + restart fixed the main cause. bringing weight back to the target group slowly.
Mike Chen: incrementally adding targets back 10% at a time. error rate holding steady ~0.5% (baseline 0.1%).
Simone (product): updating support and status page: short blip in API responses for ~10-15 minutes starting 14:02 UTC, partial traffic failures, mitigation in progress. please include guidance on retry/backoff for customers.
Sasha Rivera: creating incident notes: root cause — partial certificate rotation failure left stale certs on some backend instances, causing mutual TLS handshake failures and ALB target unhealthy flapping; mitigation — remove failing targets, weighted failover to warm pool, rolling restart to pick up new certs. next actions — investigate rotation job failure on those nodes, add more robust post-rotation healthchecks, and add a canary test that exercises mTLS after rotation.
Anya Patel: filing follow-up ticket in infra: INFRA-4729 "cert-rotation missed nodes - investigate cron/restart edgecases". tagging netops and infra.
Sasha Rivera: handing off to Leo for postmortem and remediation. Leo you're on the follow-up and next-day oncall?
Leo Gomez: got it. I'll own the postmortem and coordinate fix. I'll also add an automated alert for cert expiry mismatch across target group.
Simone (product): thanks everyone — I'm drafting status update to customers and will send a short note once postmortem ETA exists.
Sasha Rivera: closing the active pager. watch for regressions. if error rate goes back above 1% I'll reopen. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident #INC-2987 marked RESOLVED by Sasha Rivera.
Leo Gomez: follow-up checklist: postmortem, rotation job audit, add mTLS canary, and add alert for certificate mismatch across TGs. I'll update INFRA-4729 with proposed remediation and timeline.
Simone (product): leaving this thread open for postmortem link. thanks all. :raised_hands:
